_hint: Copy-edit checkpoint template. Copy to `.claude/<handoff-name>.json`, delete every `_hint` key after first fill. This is a snapshot of state between sessions, not an append-only log — it gets REWRITTEN WHOLE on 'checkpoint', not appended to. Mechanics: PIPELINE §11.
updated: <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp, from `date -u` or `git show -s --format=%cI`, never hand-typed>

identity.role: <e.g. 'tech lead, main chat with the owner'>
identity.contract: <one line: what this chat commits to vs. what the orchestrator commits to>
identity.models: <model per role, e.g. 'lead: Opus - orchestrator: Opus in Claude Code - subagents: an explicitly named model, R6'>
identity.terminology: <pointer to the project's own term glossary, rather than restating it here>
identity.handoff_ownership: <which sections of this file which role may edit, e.g. 'orchestrator appends current_state.<id> blocks; lead edits identity and awaiting_owner only'>

current_state.status: <one line: what is in flight right now>
history_compact: <one line per closed epic/train, oldest first: id - one-line result - hash/tag if applicable>
current_state._hint_active_blocks: One nested object per active epic or train is appended here by the orchestrator as work proceeds, keyed by its own id (e.g. "epic_slug" or "train_slug"). Keys inside each block are free-form per epic - brief pointer, order, status, blockers. A closed epic's block moves into history_compact as one line instead of staying here in full.

<epic_or_train_id>.brief_pointer: <path to the brief/chain-brief this block tracks>

incidents_open: <one line per open incident: what broke, current mitigation, owner of the fix>
awaiting_owner: <one line per decision the cycle is blocked on: what is being asked, what the options are>
next_session_first_steps: 1. Read THIS file, then the project's own entry-point doc.
3. <standard resume path, e.g. 'continue the chain from its last RESUME line'>

tooling_notes.checkpoint_channel: <how this file gets written, e.g. 'filesystem write, verified by re-read'; name a dead channel explicitly if one exists so nobody retries it>
tooling_notes.version_sources: <list of files that must move in lockstep on a version bump>
tooling_notes.build: <wrapper scripts to use; never the bare toolchain directly>
tooling_notes.needs_restart: <tools whose long-lived process must restart to see a recent change, or 'none'>

patterns_reminder: <short list of the project's own hard invariants that must not be violated silently - a pointer to the canonical doc is better than restating them here>
